first_impression.summary_in_own_words: A destination guide to getting married in Portugal, with a planning service called Wedded Concierge behind it. It tells me the regions, the legal minimum and the seasons straight away. It names couples from the US and UK as well as Australia, so it is not just for Australians. What I cannot tell yet is whether this is a full-service destination wedding planner or a booking concierge, and who the senior people are.

attention_map.quote: Wedded Concierge plans weddings in Portugal for couples from Australia, the United States and the United Kingdom, with one Wedded Advisor from first enquiry to the wedding weekend.
attention_map.why: Good: one person end to end is what I want, and the US and UK are named. But the page title says Wedded Wonderland and this says Wedded Concierge and Wedded Advisor. Three brand names in the first screen, and I am not sure which one I would be hiring.

attention_map.quote: Not a wedding? Ask us about a Madeira or Azores honeymoon, a Douro anniversary or a Sintra proposal.
attention_map.why: In the first screen this reads like a travel agent that does everything, not a specialist destination wedding planner.
Too early for me to hand over details. I have not seen any proof yet.

attention_map.quote: Planned by Wedded Concierge, with one Wedded Advisor from enquiry to the wedding weekend.
attention_map.why: This is where I look for proof. No numbers, no names, no press, nothing. It just repeats the line from the hero.

attention_map.quote: Romantic palaces in the Sintra hills that can be booked for a wedding
attention_map.why: Specific and appealing. The Monserrate scaffolding note to 2027 is honest, and that kind of detail is what I want a planner to catch.

An airport for every region is useful for guest travel. But every card says 'Guests: Ask your Wedded Advisor' and 'spring and autumn, as a national guide', so five cards say the same thing. No drive times at all, and that is my real question.

attention_map.quote: state events can cancel bookings at Queluz or the National Palace of Sintra. Nothing may be fixed to the heritage.
attention_map.why: The kind of detail that makes me think someone knows the ground. I would want my planner to explain the cancellation risk to me.

attention_map.quote: Easy to reach on three passports
attention_map.why: Fine, but I already knew we do not need a visa.

attention_map.quote: exclusive use can mean paying for rooms your guests do not fill.
attention_map.why: The most useful block for us. It sounds like a planner protecting our budget. It is the closest the page comes to talking about money.

attention_map.quote: Your Wedded Advisor walks you through the exact route for your nationality.
attention_map.why: Thorough and well sourced, and the US paragraph is clearly written for us. But it is a lot of government detail. I would expect the planner to handle this, not hand me seven links. I scanned it for 'we handle the paperwork' and did not find it.

attention_map.quote: Many Lisbon-area venues are 15 to 30 minutes from the city centre, as a guide
attention_map.why: The only travel time on the page, and it is for Lisbon only. Nothing for the Douro or the Algarve, which is where we would want to know whether it is within two hours of an airport.

attention_map.quote: What a wedding in Portugal costs depends on five things: your guest count, the region, the season, how many nights you take the venue and whether you book it for exclusive use. Your Wedded Advisor talks you through the options for your plans.
attention_map.why: A tab called Costs with no cost in it. Nothing on how you charge, whether supplier costs are passed through, or what currency. I have read this sentence on every planner site that does not want to tell me.

attention_map.quote: There is no set Portugal package. Instead, your Wedded Advisor helps you plan a weekend around your guests, and it can include:
attention_map.why: 'Can include' and 'helps you plan' are not 'we handle'. 'An on-the-day coordinator' is listed as something the weekend can include, which tells me you might not be there on the day. This is the end-to-end question and it is hedged.

attention_map.quote: Guest website in Wonderland Studio: share the schedule, travel and entry rules in one place. [Start for free]
attention_map.why: Another brand name, and a free DIY tool. That pulls against full service.
Not for me. More of the 'we do everything' feel.

attention_map.quote: Shape your weekend. Together you shortlist venues and plan the weekend, with the same Wedded Advisor from first enquiry to the wedding weekend.
attention_map.why: This is where I expected a name, a face and how senior they are. Instead it is a role title. It never says who designs the day, who books and manages suppliers, or who is on site. 'Portugal properties are still being confirmed' in Wedded Privileges makes it sound like you are only just setting up here.
No idea when, or how senior they are. The form itself is short and fine.

attention_map.quote: How much is an average wedding in Portugal? ... There is no single average
attention_map.why: Same non-answer as the Costs tab. The palace and beach answers are good.

attention_map.quote: Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez's wedding
attention_map.why: Celebrity gossip links on a page where you show me none of your own weddings. It makes the site feel like a wedding magazine, not a planning firm.

questions_answered.question: What exactly does end-to-end include?
questions_answered.evidence: 'one Wedded Advisor from first enquiry to the wedding weekend', a weekend that 'can include' venue nights, dinners, ceremony, party, brunch and 'An on-the-day coordinator', and the contract checks. Supplier booking, design, guest logistics and being on site are never stated as yours to do.

questions_answered.question: Why an Australian company for a wedding in Europe?
questions_answered.evidence: The page never says where the firm is based or why it suits a US or UK couple. Australian passports are listed first everywhere and Canberra and Smartraveller turn up, so I can sense the Australian base but nothing addresses it.

questions_answered.question: How far is it from a major airport?
questions_answered.evidence: Each region has its nearest airport, and 'Many Lisbon-area venues are 15 to 30 minutes from the city centre, as a guide'. No transfer times for the Algarve, Douro, Comporta or Madeira.

questions_answered.question: How are fees and supplier costs structured, and in what currency?
questions_answered.evidence: Costs tab and FAQ 4 only list what drives cost and say 'Your Wedded Advisor talks you through the options'. Nothing about the planner fee, supplier pass-through or currency. Even the registry fee is just 'charges a fee'.

questions_answered.question: Can we see weddings you have done here?
questions_answered.evidence: No real weddings anywhere on the live page. The only weddings shown are celebrity ones in the Trending row.

objections_triggered.objection: No proof they have planned weddings in Portugal
objections_triggered.triggered_by: Proof strip with no numbers, no real weddings, a Trending row of celebrity weddings, and 'Portugal properties are still being confirmed'
'Your Wedded Advisor talks you through the options for your plans.'

objections_triggered.objection: Scope reads as advisory, not full service
objections_triggered.triggered_by: 'helps you plan a weekend around your guests, and it can include', 'An on-the-day coordinator', 'Start for free'

objections_triggered.objection: No senior people named; worried replies will be slow or junior
objections_triggered.triggered_by: 'Your Wedded Advisor is your one contact at Wedded Concierge' and 'A Wedded Advisor will reply.'

objections_triggered.objection: Why use a firm based in Australia?
objections_triggered.triggered_by: Never addressed. Australian passports listed first, Canberra and Smartraveller references
Airport codes only, with no transfer times outside Lisbon

trust_signals_noticed: Detailed, sourced legal steps for US and UK passports, 'Checked October 2026'
Sintra palace booking conditions, including state-event cancellations and the Monserrate roof works
Venue contract checklist: rooms, buy-outs, per guest or per day minimums, VAT
US and UK couples named in the brand sentence
turn_offs_noticed: No named senior planner, no faces, no press
No real weddings, celebrity gossip links instead
Too many brand names: Wedded Wonderland, Wedded Concierge, Wedded Advisor, Wonderland Studio, Wedded Privileges
Honeymoon, proposal and birthday offers dilute the planner message
No reply time on the form

emotional_response.overall: Reassured that the research is careful, but cold. Nothing tells me a person here would care about our day.
emotional_response.emotionally_invested_signal: None. No voice, no story, no planner talking to us.

payload.decision_reason: I would keep the tab for the Sintra palace rules and the legal steps, because they are better than most. I would not enquire. My threshold is clear scope, proof and fees, and the page gives me none of the three: no weddings you have done in Portugal, no named senior planner, nothing on how you charge or in what currency, and 'can include' wording where I want 'we handle'. Next to a planner tab with a portfolio and a fee page, this loses.
payload.verbatim_reaction: This is a really well researched guide, honestly better than the planners' sites on the legal side. But I came for a full-service destination wedding planner and I still do not know who you are. Who is my Wedded Advisor? Have you actually done a wedding in Portugal? How do you charge? Instead of our own weddings I get Ronaldo's. I would bookmark it for the palace rules and go and enquire with someone who shows me their work.
